family: The single total prefix-data language in proof.md, family.py and engine.py. At small lengths or a failed explicit parameter guard it uses the legacy certificate-prefix evaluator. At all sufficiently large actual lengths N it uses the exact integer-rounded Shaltiel challenge-response construction with k=2^ceil((ceil(log2 N))^(19/25)) and elementary odd-degree cubic base fields with charged input-prefix field moduli and traversing matrices. All good-data choices are actual input bits; invalid data still give bounded quotient-ring and matrix evaluation. The payload is zero-padded injectively. No per-length advice or uncharged construction data are used.
theorem: This fixed total language is in P, hence NP with empty witnesses. Unconditionally in the pinned full B2 model, for every sufficiently large integer actual length N, C_B2(F_N)>=(7/2)*N-2^((log2 N)^(77/100)). More strongly, for every real epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(F_N)>=(7/2)*N-N^epsilon for every integer N>=N_epsilon, for this SAME family. The exact eventual loss is R(N)=(7/2)*P(N)+(13/2)*k(N)=N^o(1), including all P(N) prefix bits, as proved in proof.md and the supplied disperser arguments.
